# Terex Equipment Guide at CTOS


When you need Terex equipment, it’s important to find a strategic partner with the inventory, locations and support to back it up. Custom Truck One Source is a full Terex Utilities distributor with locations across the U.S. and Canada, a rental fleet of more than 10,000 units and the parts depth to keep your crew moving. Whether you’re buying, renting or sourcing parts, here’s how we deliver on Terex.


## Terex Equipment for Sale and Rent


Custom Truck One Source carries both Terex Utilities’ primary product lines, including aerial devices and digger derricks, across new, used and rental inventory. Whether you’re building out a fleet or need a unit ready to roll for a specific project, we have the equipment you need.


### Terex Bucket Trucks and Aerial Devices


Our Terex aerial lineup spans a wide range of working heights, configurations and applications. The Hi-Ranger, Optima, TL-series and HR-series models are widely relied upon for electric utility line work, telecom installation and right-of-way maintenance. Working heights range from approximately 34 feet on the compact T292 up to 60 feet on the HR55 and TC55 Optima. Material handling capacities reach 2,000 pounds on select models for crews that need to lift and work simultaneously.


For jobs in rough or low-access terrain, tracked configurations bring that same Terex aerial capability off-road. The TM100 mounted on a Morooka MST 3500 reaches


[working heights of 100 feet](https://www.customtruck.com/track-equipment/terex-tm100-morooka-3500-tracked-bucket-truck/) , and the TM125 on a Prinoth GT-4500 crawler carrier tops out at 125 feet. These units go where conventional bucket trucks cannot.


Custom Truck One Source carries new Terex bucket trucks for sale and maintains a deep Terex-weighted rental fleet for both short-term and extended deployments.


### Terex Digger Derricks


Terex digger derricks have been the go-to tool for distribution and transmission line installation for more than 80 years. Custom Truck One Source carries the Commander and General series across new inventory, with units ready for a range of utility contractor and IOU applications.


The


[Commander 4047 offers](https://www.customtruck.com/diggers/terex-commander-4047/) a max sheave height of 47.4 feet, a max horizontal reach of 37.5 feet and a lifting capacity of 24,750 pounds, purpose-built for distribution work where productivity and positioning matter. For heavy transmission jobs, the


[General 80 tracked digger derrick](https://www.customtruck.com/diggers/terex-general-80-track/) delivers a sheave height of 80.3 feet and a lifting capacity of up to 48,790 pounds, mounted on a Prinoth GT-4500 crawler carrier for access in demanding terrain.


Across the Terex derrick lineup, the dual-hydraulic-lift-cylinder construction delivers the stability and lifting performance that transmission and distribution crews depend on.

The 24/7 support call center means you’re not waiting until business hours to start the process — whatever you need, you can start the conversation with us any time.


Whether it’s a routine service component or a hard-to-find part for an older model,


[we have the inventory depth](https://www.customtruck.com/parts) and coast-to-coast reach to move quickly.


## About Terex Utilities


Terex Utilities is a subsidiary of Terex Corporation, a global manufacturer whose portfolio spans multiple equipment categories and brands, including Genie aerial work platforms and Powerscreen materials processing equipment. Within that broader family, Terex Utilities focuses specifically on the electric utility industry, manufacturing the bucket trucks and digger derricks that build and maintain the power grid across North America.


The company’s roots go back to 1945, when it introduced the first hydraulic digger derrick — the start of more than 80 years of utility equipment manufacturing. Terex units are engineered to the specifications of the utilities and contractors that depend on them in the field.


Terex is known for its fiberglass boom winding process — producing booms that are strong, rigid, and built to hold up under demanding field conditions. The dual-cylinder construction of Terex digger derricks provides superior stability under load, which is why these units remain widely relied upon across distribution and transmission work. Each piece of equipment is built to customer specifications, not an assembly-line standard.
